Both ChromaDB memory search methods apply an inclusive lower-bound filter: search_similar_usage has `if similarity_score >= similarity_threshold:` at src/sqllens/agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py:251, and search_text_memories has the identical pattern `if similarity_score >= similarity_threshold:` at agent_memory.py:423. This is a widen-not-replace filter (score at or above the bar passes). The caller in src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py:94-131 relies exactly on this: it computes `text_search_floor = min(context_floor, strict)` (line 102) and passes it to search_text_memories (line 111), and passes the lower `context_floor` to search_similar_usage (line 123), then client-side filters `r.similarity_score < strict` (line 128) to carve out just the new lower band from the widened candidate set. This only works because the backend threshold is a lower bound that returns a superset when given a lower floor, confirming the claim.

For any pair with context_similarity_threshold >= similarity_threshold, band_enabled is always False (so search_similar_usage never runs) and text_search_floor = min(context_floor, strict) = strict, i.e. it tracks similarity_threshold's actual value (not hard-coded 0.7) for any equal/non-default pair, e.g. both=0.5 gives text_search_floor=0.5 and band_enabled=False. This matches the docstring's universal claim at lines 51-56.

src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py:121-131: search_similar_usage is called with similarity_threshold=context_floor (the lower band floor), and its implementation (src/sqllens/agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py:251) returns any hit with similarity_score >= similarity_threshold — no upper bound — so tool_hits can legitimately include pairs whose similarity_score >= strict. However, band_pairs (the only tool-pair list actually rendered, at default.py:146-151) is built via the comprehension `[r for r in tool_hits if r.similarity_score < strict and isinstance(r.memory.args, dict) and r.memory.args.get('sql')]` (default.py:125-131), which strictly excludes every result with similarity_score >= strict (using < strict, so scores exactly equal to strict are also excluded). tool_hits itself is never rendered or used elsewhere. Therefore no pair scoring at or above the strict bar can reach the injected band section, matching the comment's claim exactly.

The render loop at lines 146-151 then iterates only over band_pairs and subscripts `pair.args['sql']` at line 150, which is safe because every element already passed the truthy-sql filter.
